revisions.prompt:
Use case: precise-object-edit. Asset: existing snowball-game background.
Image 1 is the EDIT TARGET, the current high-resolution snowfield. Image 2 is the ORIGINAL GAME composition/orientation reference.
Fix only the UPPER-LEFT snow fort in image 1. It is facing the wrong way. Turn its horseshoe/C-shaped snow wall 180 degrees on the ground so its opening faces UPPER LEFT (northwest), away from the field centre. Its continuous rounded convex OUTSIDE wall must face LOWER RIGHT, toward the opposing fort. Match the upper-left fort's orientation in image 2: foreground/lower-right is a continuous snowy curved wall, and the hollow/opening is behind that wall toward the upper-left. Do not leave two forts facing the same direction.
Preserve this fort's centre, overall footprint, scale, camera and smooth sculpted powder material; redraw lighting so it still matches the same scene light. Keep the LOWER-RIGHT fort, all remaining snowfield pixels, empty centre, outer snowbanks, colour palette, lighting, aspect ratio and overall composition unchanged. No characters, text, interface, extra objects or new forts. Full opaque landscape background.

Use case: precise-object-edit. Asset: snowball-game background.
Edit this image to REMOVE the entire raised circular/oval snowbank that rings the outside of the field. Replace that whole perimeter with the same low, flat, softly textured open snow as the playable field, continuing naturally off all four image edges. No circular rim, surrounding mound, border, bowl, crater, enclosing wall, circular shading/vignette, or arena outline.
Preserve BOTH interior snow forts exactly as shown: the upper-left C-shaped fort opens toward upper-left and has a continuous convex foreground wall; the lower-right fort opens toward lower-right. Keep their exact positions, sizes, camera, materials, lighting and opposing orientations. Preserve the broad empty snowfield between them, the wide aspect ratio and smoothly shaded tactile high-resolution 2.5D winter illustration. Quiet near-white snow with subtle natural powder texture and faint cool daylight shading. No people, extra objects, labels, interface, text or watermark. Opaque landscape background.

Use case: precise-object-edit. Asset: snowball-game background.
Add a sparse, naturally irregular scattering of small snow-covered EVERGREEN TREES along the OUTERMOST edges of this snowfield. About 8 trees total, asymmetrically distributed around the top, bottom, left and right edges/corners, with varied small sizes and spacing; a few may be partly cropped by the image edge. Restrict trunks and crowns to a narrow outer perimeter (roughly the outermost 7% of the canvas) so the central playable snow remains completely unobstructed. Trees should read as small background boundary scenery, with max visible height around 10% of image height; no giant foreground trees. Dark green soft rounded layered fir branches with generous powder caps and short cool, softly feathered contact shadows. Match the same slightly overhead camera, tactile smooth 2.5D winter-game materials, daylight direction and snow scale.
Preserve both forts EXACTLY: their positions, sizes, shapes and opposing orientations. Upper-left fort opens upper-left, lower-right fort opens lower-right. Preserve all empty snow between forts. Keep the field flat and open; do NOT add a circular mound, snowbank ring, enclosing wall, border or circular vignette. No extra forts, rocks, fences, paths, buildings, people, characters, UI, text or watermark. Full opaque landscape image.

Use case: precise-object-edit. Asset: existing snowball-game playfield background.
REMOVE every scattered tree currently at the top, bottom, left and right edges. Restore flat softly textured open snow everywhere those trees stood.
Instead create ONE attractive clustered grove of 4 or 5 snow-covered evergreen Christmas trees ONLY in the TOP-RIGHT CORNER of the image. Arrange varied heights naturally as one coherent group near the corner, some branches lightly cropped at the top/right edge. Keep the whole grove within roughly the rightmost 18% of the image and topmost 20%, far from both forts and the central playable area. Make it a polished outdoor Christmas scene: thick powder snow resting on layered evergreen branches, warm glowing outdoor string lights wound around the trees, tasteful red and gold weatherproof baubles, a few subtle garlands and small star toppers. Lights should glow gently in daytime snow, not turn the scene into night. This should look like a lovely decorated woodland corner, not a line of isolated trees or a fence.
Match the existing smooth tactile 2.5D winter game illustration, slightly overhead camera, powder materials and daylight. Add soft realistic cool contact shadows under the grove.
Keep BOTH snow forts pixel-positioned as in the input, with their exact scale, shape and opposing directions. Preserve all other snowfield texture and the large clear central play space. No circular mound, enclosing snowbank or perimeter border. No trees anywhere outside the single top-right group. No people, animals, buildings, text, UI or watermark. Opaque wide landscape.
